messages:
maya: Customer reported sudden 429s after org migration. New API key rolled, same NAT IP. They saw a burst window that lasted ~2m. I can repro from our NAT.

maya: Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_new_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hi"}'
```

raj: Checking edge logs — rate-limiter attributed requests to the old org for a short time due to missing/rewritten auth header at ingress. Sample log:
```
[2026-02-11T12:34:05Z] INFO  src=10.12.4.5 key= - org=org_OLD rate_bucket=ip:10.12.4.5:global count=120
[2026-02-11T12:34:06Z] INFO  src=10.12.4.5 key=sk_new_abc org=org_NEW rate_bucket=ip:10.12.4.5:global count=121
```

emma: The limiter's attribution order is: API key -> session token -> source IP. If header parsing fails during our ALB rollout, we fall back to IP. Looks like header truncation due to header-size limit in the ingress config. Will raise a small patch to increase header buffer.

maya: Steps I used: hit generate concurrently from two projects (old org and new org) but with same NAT. When key header is missing on some requests they got credited to the IP bucket and tripped 429s for both orgs.

raj: Quick mitigation: set the request header `X-Redwood-Affinity: key` to force per-key mapping on edge for affected customers (edge will prefer key mapping if present). Also we can add a per-tenant override so IP buckets aren't shared during migrations.

maya: Workaround sent to customer, they confirmed reduced 429s after adding header. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rolled out hotfix to ingress config increasing header buffer and a rate-limiter preference change (prefer-key-over-ip) to control plane in canary (edge-3).

samu: Note for migration playbook: remind customers to rotate keys during low traffic and recommend X-Redwood-Affinity header for staged cutovers. Also plan to credit customer for the affected minute window.

raj: Follow-up: will add an automated detector to flag org-migration patterns (same NAT, different keys) so support can preemptively apply per-tenant override.

maya: Thanks — closing this thread, filing a support follow-up doc.
